overview: Slice files into 8 MiB parts and upload at most three concurrently. Confirm progress only for acknowledged parts; in-flight bytes are provisional. Store session metadata in IndexedDB, not the whole file by default; after reload require re-selection and verify fingerprint unless a supported permissioned file handle is available. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.calculation: ~24 MiB active chunk payload plus browser/network overhead
estimation.result: Bound concurrency and release buffers; actual browser copies add memory
estimation.implication: Profile peak memory and progress behavior with retries, pause and background tabs.

Performance plan: Up to 2 GiB per file; three concurrent 8 MiB parts; no whole-file ArrayBuffer. steps.title: Receive user intent
steps.explanation: Validate files and create per-file upload sessions. Provide a labelled file input as well as drag/drop, keyboard pause/cancel, text progress and throttled announcements. Validation errors identify the affected file.

steps.title: Render controlled child state
steps.explanation: Up to 2 GiB per file; three concurrent 8 MiB parts; no whole-file ArrayBuffer. Child events return to the owner; focus and selection use stable identities.

steps.title: Call or subscribe to the feature dependency
steps.explanation: Persist resumable session identity and acknowledgements separately from ephemeral File references. Reconcile confirmed parts from server; retry the same part number/checksum safely. Expired sessions require explicit restart; cancel aborts active requests and informs the server.

steps.title: Capture user intent without duplicating authority
steps.explanation: Validate local input and enter a pending state. Use the component callback rather than mutating server snapshots directly.

steps.title: Send the versioned operation
steps.explanation: Call POST /uploads through the API adapter. Request: {name:"demo.mp4",size:2147483648,mime:"video/mp4",fingerprint:"..."}. A prior successful response or unresolved operation must not be overwritten by a stale retry.

steps.title: Reconcile or expose recovery
steps.explanation: Reconcile confirmed parts from server; retry the same part number/checksum safely. Expired sessions require explicit restart; cancel aborts active requests and informs the server. Update the query key with the acknowledged version or invalidate/refetch it; maintain focus and make pending/error state visible.

steps.title: Create the session
steps.explanation: Use the existing POST /uploads contract to receive part size and scoped signed destinations. Persist session metadata; slice without reading the whole file.

steps.title: Upload bounded parts
steps.explanation: At most three PUT requests stream 8 MiB slices. Record confirmed part numbers/ETags; a timed-out acknowledgement triggers session reconciliation before retry.

steps.title: Finalize the asset
steps.explanation: Submit the confirmed manifest after every required part is acknowledged. Show processing until the server reports the asset ready; cancellation must prevent automatic completion.

failureCases.scenario: A part succeeds but its acknowledgement times out
failureCases.handling: Reconcile confirmed parts from server; retry the same part number/checksum safely. Expired sessions require explicit restart; cancel aborts active requests and informs the server.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
